findings.claim: Activity 3 now places the request in development behind the Vite dev proxy (line 551), but report 2 still says "a gateway answers 502 with an HTML page". When the proxy target is down, Vite's own proxy error handler answers 502 with Content-Type text/plain and an empty body, not an HTML page. The keyed option C still handles it identically (non-problem type, else branch, no parsing), and the original code still lands in catch (res.json() on an empty body rejects with SyntaxError), so the key and every explanation stay correct; only the scenario detail is imprecise for the stated setup.
findings.recommendation: Either say "the Vite proxy answers 502 with a plain-text body" (and refer to "the gateway's non-JSON body" in the option B and C explanations), or say the outage happens in production behind a same-origin gateway that returns an HTML 502 page.

items.note: Line 551 now fixes the setup: VITE_API_URL is /api and the Vite dev proxy forwards it to Spring Boot, so the request is same-origin and the fulfilled-400/502 claims hold. Recap line 660 now says fetch rejects on a network failure or a CORS-blocked cross-origin response, the cheat sheet (line 666) says a rejection means no readable response, and the Using Fetch source note mentions CORS; artifact.md mirrors these. Earlier Chromium run: a same-origin 502 fulfilled, a cross-origin 502 without CORS headers rejected (TypeError: Failed to fetch).

Recap line 657 limits setAttribute to harmless attributes such as data- (never an event handler, href or src), and option D (line 434) says setAttribute on a data- attribute stores only a value; MDN setAttribute is now a listed source. Re-executed in Chromium: the new onmouseover payload ran on hover via innerHTML and via insertAdjacentHTML, and created no anchor via textContent. Click on the CSS-drawn icon span: target SPAN.icon, matches("button.like") false, closest() found the li id; click on the word: target BUTTON; currentTarget.dataset.id undefined. So keyed D is the only correct option and A/B/C explanations are accurate.
Option C explanation (line 619) now ends "a network failure still reaches the connection message in catch", which no longer claims catch is reached only by a rejected fetch.
